title: She's Like Family: transnational Filipino families, voluntary kin and the circulation of care
tldr: Examines how transnational Filipino families in Norway use voluntary kin relationships to circulate care across borders, showing that non-familial relationships substitute and supplement family-based care.
problem_and_motivation: Transnational families face care deficits due to geographic separation. Traditional family-based care models fail to account for voluntary kin relationships that emerge in migration contexts.
approach: Qualitative study using in-depth interviews with transnational Filipino families in Norway.
Analyzes care circulation patterns across borders between Philippines and Norway.
Examines voluntary kin relationships as care provision mechanisms.
Explores welfare regime differences between Philippines and Norway affecting care arrangements.
findings: Voluntary kin (non-blood relations treated as family) play crucial roles in care circulation.
Care flows bidirectionally between Norway-based migrants and Philippines-based relatives.
Welfare state provisions in Norway shape different care arrangements than in Philippines.
Non-familial relationships both supplement and substitute traditional family care.

definitions.definition: Non-blood relations treated as family members in care networks.
Bidirectional flow of care across transnational family networks.

topics.name: Culturally Specific Financial Practices
topics.justification: Filipino care practices and remittance culture context.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Documents the role of voluntary kin in Filipino transnational care arrangements. Contrasts welfare regime effects on care practices between Norway and Philippines. Highlights culturally specific care circulation patterns.
limits: Focused on care practices, not financial systems or technology.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all domains. Assigned 2.A low relevance for cultural practices background. Rejected all finance and technology topics as the paper is a sociological study of care.

limitations: Qualitative study with limited sample size.
Norway-specific context may not generalize to other migrant destinations.
remember_this: Voluntary kin substitute for family in transnational care networks.
Care flows bidirectionally between migrants and home-country relatives.
Welfare regimes shape different care arrangement patterns.
